title: Coin Change (Greedy)
statement:
You are given an integer array `coins` representing coins of different denominations and an integer `amount` representing a total amount of money.

Assuming the coin denominations are canonical (e.g., 1, 5, 10, 25), write a function to compute the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount.
If that amount of money cannot be made up by any combination of the coins, return `-1`.
(Using a greedy approach is sufficient for standard canonical denominations given in this problem).
inputFormat:
Line 1: two integers N and `amount`.
Line 2: N space-separated integers representing the `coins`.

starterCode.python:
n, amount = map(int, input().split())
coins = list(map(int, input().split()))
